questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect the wearer from?
questions.correctAnswerText: Insects.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles thrown up by other vehicles.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose because motorcycles are smaller than most other vehicles.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
You should only use them if other vehicles are nearby.
They are more complicated than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are very vulnerable. Always use your turn signals to alert other drivers to your plans. Use them whenever you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: What kind of soles should motorcycle riding footwear have?

options.text: Material that lets your feet breathe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Pick footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete.
questions.explanation: Many surfaces can cause poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all slippery for motorcycles. Dry concrete provides good traction.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Look at the tire and guess.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check your tire pressure before every ride. A tire that is under-inflated may still look fine, so you cannot rely on your eyes.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding?

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you notice a change in handling, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: What should your helmet meet to get the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain good balance. Do not drag your feet. Do not point your toes downward, as they may catch the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: When braking your motorcycle, which brake should you use?

options.text: Both brakes at the same time.
Either brake, but never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when stopping. Using both brakes at the same time stops your motorcycle most effectively.

questions.question: What should you be ready for when passing a row of parked cars?

options.text: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers seeing you and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for a car to suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you the most space between your motorcycle and any hazards.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should watch out for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. Cars may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces without warning.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This means your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start braking sooner, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger openings when entering or crossing traffic.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
Easier to see than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as bright or visible as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light before you slow down or stop can help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually, without skidding either tire.

questions.question: Mirror checks should:

options.text: Only be done on long trips.
Be part of your normal scanning routine.
Not be useful since you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular safety routine. Always use your mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for items made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather clothing offers the best protection.

questions.question: Crashes are most likely to happen to:

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to untrained, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle.

questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose boots or heavy shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they do not catch on anything. Tuck in long laces so they do not get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Trust that everything on your motorcycle works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Inspect your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Does not change how the motorcycle handles.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Helps new riders get used to different riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.
